items.section_title: 11.3 · Objective c — Determining rate, rhythm, PR, QRS, QT and QTc
items.html: Regular or irregular. When the same distance separates every pair of consecutive R waves, the rhythm is regular; when the R to R intervals differ from beat to beat, the rhythm is irregular.
cites: 11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 54, 55
11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 54, 56

src.question: A 34-year-old man's strip is shown. How is its regularity best described?
src.explanation: The same distance separates every pair of consecutive R waves, so the rhythm is regular.

also.explanation: The R to R intervals differ from beat to beat (the gaps between consecutive complexes are visibly unequal), so the rhythm is irregular.

items.section_title: 11.3 · Objective c — Determining rate, rhythm, PR, QRS, QT and QTc
items.html: The six-second method, worked. Fourteen QRS complexes in six seconds, multiplied by ten, gives a ventricular rate of 140 per minute.
cites: 11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 44, 46

src.question: A 29-year-old woman's monitor prints this six-second strip. What is her ventricular rate?
src.explanation: Fourteen QRS complexes in six seconds, multiplied by ten, gives a ventricular rate of 140 per minute.

items.section_title: 11.3 · Objective c — Determining rate, rhythm, PR, QRS, QT and QTc
items.html: The 300 method, worked. Divide 300 by the large boxes between consecutive R waves: 300 divided by four is 75 per minute, and 300 divided by six large boxes is 50 per minute, below 60 and so a bradycardia.
cites: 11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 52, 53
11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 52, 77

src.question: A 47-year-old woman's regular strip is shown; consecutive R waves sit four large boxes apart. What is the rate by the 300 method (normal 60 to 100 per minute)?
src.explanation: The 300 method divides 300 by the large boxes between consecutive R waves: 300 divided by four is 75 per minute.

also.explanation: By the 300 method, 300 divided by six large boxes is 50 per minute (this strip measures about 51), below 60 and so a bradycardia.

items.section_title: 11.6 · Objective f — Sinus bradycardia, sinus tachycardia and sinus arrhythmia
items.html: Only the rate differs. Normal sinus rhythm, sinus bradycardia and sinus tachycardia are all regular with normal P waves married to the QRS and a normal PR; only the ventricular rate (under 60, 60 to 100, over 100) differs.
cites: 11. Rhythm Analysis and Sinus Rhythm.pptx, Slides 72, 75, 78

src.question: A 57-year-old woman asks how normal sinus rhythm, sinus bradycardia and sinus tachycardia differ. What separates them?
src.explanation: All three are regular with normal P waves married to the QRS and a normal PR; only the ventricular rate (under 60, 60 to 100, over 100) differs.

items.html: Trigeminy. Every third beat is a premature complex: two normal beats then an early one, repeating.
cites: 12. Ectopy, Escape Rhythms and Supraventricular Dysrhythmias.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: A 55-year-old woman's lead II strip is shown. What pattern do her premature beats follow?
src.explanation: Every third beat is a premature complex, two normal beats then an early one, repeating: trigeminy.

items.html: Quadrigeminy. Every fourth beat is a premature complex: three normal beats then an early one (here ventricular).
cites: 12. Ectopy, Escape Rhythms and Supraventricular Dysrhythmias.pptx, Slides 10, 73

src.question: A 68-year-old man's lead II strip is shown. What pattern do the wide premature beats follow?
src.explanation: Every fourth beat is a wide premature complex, three normal beats then an early one: quadrigeminy (here ventricular).

items.html: A run of consecutive wide beats. Three or more consecutive premature ventricular complexes at a fast rate are ventricular tachycardia; a brief run is nonsustained and needs evaluation.
cites: 12. Ectopy, Escape Rhythms and Supraventricular Dysrhythmias.pptx, Slides 70, 71

src.question: A 72-year-old man's strip is shown, with a short run of consecutive wide beats. What does the run represent?
src.explanation: Three or more consecutive premature ventricular complexes at a fast rate are ventricular tachycardia; a brief run like this one is nonsustained and needs evaluation.

items.section_title: 12.6 · Objective f — Recognizing the supraventricular dysrhythmias
items.html: Counting flutter waves. Draw a line through the peaks of the flutter waves and count the troughs until the next QRS complex; that number sets the ratio.
cites: 12. Ectopy, Escape Rhythms and Supraventricular Dysrhythmias.pptx, Slides 26, 27

src.question: A 67-year-old man's flutter ratio is unclear. How are the flutter waves counted?
src.key: Count troughs to the next QRS
src.explanation: Draw a line through the peaks of the flutter waves and count the troughs until the next QRS complex; that number sets the ratio.

items.html: The systematic approach to a 12-lead. It runs: general impression, calibration, axis, QRS assessment, hypertrophy and chamber enlargement, then ST and T wave changes.

src.question: A 61-year-old woman's 12-lead has a good general impression and standard calibration. What is assessed next?
src.explanation: The systematic approach runs: general impression, calibration, axis, QRS assessment, hypertrophy and chamber enlargement, then ST and T wave changes.

items.section_title: 14.9 · Objective i — The anatomy behind conduction blocks and chamber enlargement
items.html: Left anterior fascicular block. The left anterior hemiblock is the most common intraventricular conduction abnormality during an acute myocardial infarction.

src.question: A 62-year-old man develops a new intraventricular conduction abnormality. Which one is most common during an acute myocardial infarction?
src.explanation: Left anterior fascicular block, the left anterior hemiblock, is the most common intraventricular conduction abnormality during an acute myocardial infarction.

items.section_title: 16.3 · Objective c — Potassium and calcium on the tracing
items.html: U waves. A small wave after the T wave is a U wave; prominent U waves, with T-wave flattening, are classic signs of hypokalemia, which prolongs repolarization.
cites: 16. EKG Pericarditis Electrolytes and Other Abnormalities.pptx, Slide 38

src.question: A 45-year-old woman's leads V4 to V6 are shown. What are the arrowed waves that follow each T wave?
src.explanation: A small wave after the T wave is a U wave. Prominent U waves, with T-wave flattening, are classic signs of hypokalemia, which prolongs repolarization.
